item.title: Does Mild Anemia Associate With 3-Month Vascular Outcomes in Severe Acute Ischemic Stroke?
item.description: CONCLUSION: In patients with severe AIS requiring neurocritical care, lower Hb levels were independently associated with an increased risk of 3-month composite vascular outcomes, even at the level of mild anemia.

item.title: Enhanced radiation resistance and pre-irradiation effects of hydroxyl-containing fluorine-doped silica optical fibers at 1550 nm
item.description: This study evaluated hydroxyl (OH)-containing, fluorine (F)-doped silica optical fibers developed to enhance radiation resistance for use in high-radiation environments. Fibers with different F and OH concentrations were fabricated using the vapor-phase axial deposition (VAD) process and compared with commercial radiation-hardened fibers under gamma-ray irradiation. The fabricated fibers exhibited superior radiation resistance, with an RIA of 3.7-6.5 dB/km at 100 kGy and 1550 nm, and a...

item.title: Liver transplantation outcomes, systemic immune-inflammatory phenotype, and predictors of hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence in an HBV/HDV-endemic region: a retrospective cohort study
item.description: Chronic hepatitis B and D virus (HBV/HDV) coinfection sustains a hepatic inflammatory microenvironment from which hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) arises. Although advances in liver transplantation have improved survival, HCC recurrence remains a major challenge affecting long-term outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate post-transplant outcomes and identify risk factors associated with HCC recurrence among liver transplant recipients in Mongolia, and to characterize their pre-transplant systemic...

item.title: Biogeography and monsoon-associated climatic trait evolution in true frogs Rana
item.description: Climatic variation across latitude shapes lineage diversification and niche evolution. We integrated multilocus and genome-wide SNPs, morphological characters, historical biogeography, and phylogenetic comparative analyses for 391 sampled individuals representing 21 recognised Rana species across the Palearctic. Time-calibrated total-evidence analyses resolved three major stem lineages originating in the Early Miocene, 22.00 Mya, followed by radiations across East Asia and the central...

item.title: Cell-free DNA in human ovarian follicular fluid as a potential biomarker of embryo quality in IVF cycles: a pilot study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In women under 40, increased cfDNA fragmentation in FF was associated with lower morphology-based embryo quality. However, the observed correlations were modest, and the absence of preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A), implantation, clinical pregnancy, and live birth outcomes limits clinical interpretation. These exploratory findings do not establish FF cfDNA as a clinically validated predictive biomarker or demonstrate that it improves embryo selection. Larger...

item.title: In the Age When AI Writes Papers, What Is Left for Researchers?
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Association Between Cancer Stage and Parenting Self-Efficacy in Breast Cancer Survivors: A Survey of a Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Community
item.description: CONCLUSION: Advanced cancer stages may be associated with lower parenting self-efficacy among breast cancer survivor mothers. However, this association appears sensitive to stage grouping and warrants cautious interpretation. These findings may provide preliminary insights into post-cancer parenting experiences, although the specific study population and cross-sectional design limit generalizability. Greater attention may be needed for social reintegration into parenting for young women with...

item.title: Association of Nontraumatic Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head With Major Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Events: A Nationwide Cohort Study of Korea
item.description: CONCLUSION: In this nationwide cohort, nontraumatic ONFH was associated with an increased long-term risk of MACCEs, driven mainly by cardiovascular events. These findings suggest that nontraumatic ONFH may serve as a clinically relevant marker of increased cardiovascular risk, supporting attention to cardiovascular risk assessment in patients with ONFH.

item.title: Exploratory Pilot Randomized Crossover Study of Transcutaneous Vagus Nerve Stimulation on Sleep Quality and Mood in Healthy Adults
item.description: CONCLUSION: This exploratory pilot trial suggests that tcVNS was safe and well tolerated and may produce modest changes in subjective sleep quality in healthy adults. The absence of mood effects likely reflects low baseline symptom burden. These findings provide preliminary, hypothesis-generating evidence that stimulation parameters may warrant further investigation, and confirmation in adequately powered trials and clinical populations is required.

item.title: Machine Learning Based Plasma Proteomic Analysis Identifies Disease Differentiating Biomarkers in Atopic Dermatitis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Our study provides insight into the application of ML algorithms for disease diagnosis, and our model may be expanded to other disease contexts. Our results identify inflammatory protein biomarkers and suggest their relevance in predicting disease severity, monitoring clinical progression and future therapeutic strategies.

item.title: A Deep Learning-Based Prediction Model for Mortality in Severe COVID-19 Patients Requiring Intensive Care Unit Admission: A Multicenter Registry Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: A deep learning-based AI model was developed to support clinical decision-making in critically ill patients with COVID-19, offering an efficient and clinically practical approach to mortality risk assessment.

item.title: Validity of Actigraphy and Sleep Diary Compared With Home Polysomnography in Patients With Sleep Apnea and Insomnia Symptoms
item.description: CONCLUSION: Both actigraphy and sleep diaries showed validity relative to PSG, but their clinical use should be tailored to the underlying sleep disorder. Sleep diaries may be particularly informative in insomnia, whereas actigraphy may be relatively more useful in sleep apnea.

item.title: Relationship Between Borderline Personality Pathology and Problematic Alcohol Use in Patients With Mood Disorders
item.description: CONCLUSION: BPP-PAU associations varied by diagnosis driven by distinct affective-impulsive mechanisms. Screening BPP traits in BD II may help identify individuals at elevated risk for hazardous drinking.

item.title: Validation of the 14-Item Shortened Version of the Positive and Negative Sleep Appraisal Measure Among Shift-Working Nurses
item.description: CONCLUSION: PANSAM-14 demonstrated acceptable psychometric properties for assessing sleep-related cognitive patterns, particularly among shift-working nurses. Its brief structure and acceptable psychometric properties suggest potential utility for clinical and occupational interpretation.

item.title: Prevalence and Intervention Gaps for PTSD and CPTSD Following Interpersonal Trauma in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Systematic Review
item.description: CONCLUSION: This review highlights a diagnostic lag and research-to-practice gap in LMICs, particularly concerning the CPTSD recently introduced in ICD-11. Addressing these disparities requires prioritizing implementation science frameworks, focusing on task-shifting models, cultural tailoring of evidence-based interventions, and the integration of digital health solutions to ensure sustainable care for vulnerable survivors.

item.title: Pregnancy Risk Information Systems for Psychotropic Medications: A Practical Review for Clinical Decision-Making
item.description: CONCLUSION: Psychotropic medication use during pregnancy should be guided by individualized risk-benefit assessment, integrating drug-specific safety signals, evidence quality, exposure timing, lactation and fertility considerations, and the risks of untreated psychiatric illness.

item.title: Antibiotic Prophylaxis for Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis in Cirrhosis: A Network Meta-analysis of Randomized Trials
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Antibiotic prophylaxis is associated with lower all-cause mortality in cirrhosis with ascites, with rifaximin showing the most consistent survival benefit. However, its SBP estimate was not reproduced in blinded placebo-controlled trials, and the preventive effect against SBP attenuated over time.

item.title: Target Trial Emulation: A Practical Introduction for Hepatology Research
item.description: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are considered the gold standard for causal inference; however, in hepatology research, their feasibility is often limited by ethical constraints, long disease trajectories, and complex treatment decisions. As a result, real-world data (RWD) are increasingly used, but conventional observational analyses remain vulnerable to biases such as immortal time bias, confounding, and misalignment between clinical questions and study design. Target trial emulation (TTE)...

item.title: Mechanotransduction in Liver Fibrosis: Sinusoidal Remodeling, Mechanometabolic Coupling, and Therapeutic Implications
item.description: Liver fibrosis has traditionally been interpreted through biochemical pathways driven by chronic injury, inflammation, metabolic stress, and profibrotic cytokine signaling. However, fibrotic progression also involves mechanical remodeling of the hepatic microenvironment. This review examines mechanotransduction in liver fibrosis, with particular emphasis on the sinusoidal niche as a mechanically responsive interface. During chronic liver injury, liver sinusoidal endothelial cell defenestration,...

item.title: A Novel Competing-Risk Model Integrating Systemic Inflammation to Predict Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The KACLiF-ACLF score discriminates ACLF development with high accuracy in external validation and supports risk stratification within a competing-risk framework. Recalibrated absolute risks require independent validation before clinical implementation.

item.title: KASL Consensus Statement for Pharmacologic Treatment of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis: Focus on Semaglutide
item.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) impose a rapidly increasing hepatic and cardiometabolic burden worldwide and in Korea. Following the phase 3 ESSENCE trial, which demonstrated the histological efficacy of semaglutide in noncirrhotic MASH with fibrosis, practical guidance for routine clinical care is needed. The Korean Association for the Study of the Liver developed this expert consensus statement on semaglutide...

item.title: Corrigendum: Current status and future perspectives of liquid biopsy in non-small cell lung cancer
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Ultrasound-guided cryoablation of recurrent thyroid cancer: radiologic-pathologic correlation
item.description: Cryoablation is a minimally invasive thermal ablation modality that destroys tumor cells through intracellular ice crystal formation and osmotic injury. Although it offers theoretical advantages, its application in recurrent papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) remains limited, and the radiologic-pathologic findings of treatment response have not been well characterized. A 55-year-old male patient with biopsy-proven recurrent PTC in the left supraclavicular fossa and a history of total thyroidectomy,...

item.title: Diagnostic pitfalls leading to delayed diagnosis of human papillomavirus (HPV)-independent cervical malignancies in the era of HPV-based screening: clinicopathologic analysis of diagnostic pathways
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: HPV-IDCM remain vulnerable to delayed diagnosis in the era of HPV-based screening. Persistent abnormal cytologic findings should not be dismissed solely because HPV test results are negative. Careful correlation of cytologic, clinical, and histologic findings remains essential for timely HPV-IDCM detection.

item.title: A demographic study of pathology-proven kidney tumors at a single institution in South Korea over the past 33 years: 1991-2023
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates a long-term increase in the incidence of renal tumors in South Korea. These findings can serve as foundational data for patients with kidney tumors.

item.title: Subclassification of the undifferentiated component in early gastric cancer: the poorly differentiated tubular adenocarcinoma component is associated with lymph node metastasis and local aggressiveness
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The por component was the histologic component most consistently associated with nodal metastasis and local aggressiveness in gastric adenocarcinoma, whereas the poorly cohesive component contributed independently to ulceration. Subclassifying the undifferentiated component captures biologically distinct behavior and may help refine risk stratification for endoscopic resection.

item.title: Targeted next-generation sequencing-based mutational signature analysis in endometrial cancer: utility and limitations across molecular subtypes
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this small, clinically selected cohort, targeted NGS-based mutational signatures provided exploratory, complementary information regarding POLE-associated mutagenesis and mixed MMR-related patterns. Overlapping signature distributions, dependence on the analytical pipeline, and the use of tumor-only targeted sequencing limit case-level interpretation. Mutational signature analysis should be interpreted in conjunction with established molecular tests and should not be used as a...

item.title: From Transdermal Delivery to Immune Reprogramming: Intelligent Biomaterials for Precision Psoriasis Therapy
item.description: Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory disease that causes dysregulation of keratinocyte proliferation, IL-23/IL-17-driven immune activation, oxidative stress and impaired barrier function. Biologics and targeted small molecules have improved clinical results, but systemic administration and lack of lesion specificity limit precise, long-term control of the disease. This paper revises the concept of psoriasis therapy from transdermal drug delivery to intelligent immune...

item.title: Nanoscale Reduced-Porphyrinic Covalent Organic Frameworks with Modulated Absorption for Enhanced Photodynamic Therapy
item.description: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer an attractive platform for organizing nanophotosensitizers into ordered architectures for improving photodynamic therapy (PDT). However, the photochemical performance of conventional porphyrin-based frameworks has largely been constrained by their limited optical absorption at longer wavelength and inefficient generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report the first highly crystalline nanoscale COFs (nCOFs) incorporating reduced porphyrin...

item.title: Teletherapy for Adolescent Mental Health: A Scoping Review of Comparative Effectiveness
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Teletherapy improves adolescent anxiety and depression relative to waitlist or minimal-contact controls, although the size of the benefit is uncertain. Face-to-face comparisons are few, and their findings differ by condition, so equivalence to in-person care cannot yet be established. Condition-specific trials with face-to-face comparators are needed.

item.title: Quality of Life Outcomes From the Phase 3 Study of Atezolizumab + Bevacizumab and Chemotherapy (ATTLAS, KCSG-LU19-04) in EGFR/ALK-Mutated Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Despite impairment in symptoms commonly associated with chemotherapy, no significant between-group difference in overall QoL was detected between ABCP and PC. Stable GHS/QoL and improvement in cancer-related symptoms were observed alongside appropriate toxicity management.

item.title: Influence of process-relevant impurities on the thermodynamic equilibrium of lithium hydroxide monohydrate during antisolvent crystallization with 2-propanol
item.description: Solid-liquid equilibria (SLE) relevant to the antisolvent crystallization of lithium hydroxide monohydrate (LiOH·H(2)O) from water-2-propanol mixtures were experimentally investigated in the presence of process-relevant hydroxide and chloride impurities (NaOH, KOH, LiCl, NaCl, and KCl) at 25 °C. Solubility measurements showed that NaOH, KOH, and LiCl reduce the solubility of LiOH through the common-ion effect while remaining relatively soluble themselves, indicating favorable conditions for...

item.title: Pore-Engineered Nanostructured Hydroxyapatite Films for Regulating Protein-Material Interactions
item.description: Transparent citrate-modified hydroxyapatite nanoparticle films with tunable pore structures were fabricated through nanoparticle assembly, P123 incorporation, and controlled calcination. The films exhibited high optical transmittance (>90%) and low haze (<1%), with characteristic pore sizes of approximately 14 and 44 nm. Protein adsorption experiments revealed higher fibrinogen adsorption on large-pore films and higher hemoglobin adsorption on small-pore films. FT-IR analysis further showed...

item.title: Impact of Adjuvant Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors and Chemotherapy on Survival Outcomes in High-Risk Upper Tract Urothelial Carcinoma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Both adjuvant ICI and adjuvant chemotherapy were associated with longer DFS after radical nephroureterectomy in patients with high-risk UTUC. Longer follow-up and prospective studies are needed to assess the durability of this association and the comparative effectiveness between adjuvant ICI and adjuvant chemotherapy.

item.title: Pitfalls of Unusual Anorectal Pathology: Rectovaginal Fistula With Ectopic Vaginal Opening in Anus and Normal Urethra
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Power-conserving coupled-mode theory for high-index-contrast multiwaveguide systems from the field continuous at the interfaces
item.description: At high index contrast, coupled-mode expansions of the electric field in isolated-waveguide guided modes become inaccurate for TM polarization, because superposed modes do not satisfy the normal-component interface condition. An earlier two-waveguide theory expands the magnetic field and derives the electric field from its curl. We extend it, with an electric-field counterpart for TE polarization, to arbitrary numbers of waveguides and guided modes, choosing the expanded field by its continuity...

item.title: Front-of-package ultraprocessed warning labels: a randomized controlled trial with Chilean parents
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Overall, the addition of UPF labels to existing FOPL systems may help consumers more easily identify products as ultraprocessed and lower consumers' perceived healthfulness and purchase intentions of UPFs. UPF labels could have the largest effects when applied to UPFs that carry no or few nutrient labels.

item.title: Body weight thresholds for sexual maturation are conserved despite mild feed restriction and differences in photostimulation timing in laying hens
item.description: As the laying hen industry transitions to cage-free systems, changes in growth trajectories and body composition may influence sexual maturation. This study investigated the interaction between photostimulation (PS) timing and body weight (BW) on sexual maturation, endocrine response, and early egg production. At 12 weeks of age (woa), 600 Lohmann LSL-Lite pullets were distributed across four rooms, each containing six aviary-style pens reared under 9L:15D. From 13 weeks of age (woa), three pens...

item.title: Mechanistic targets of Internal Family Systems in the treatment of posttraumatic stress disorder
item.description: High rates of childhood trauma and PTSD commonly characterize individuals seeking care at community outpatient clinics. Growing evidence suggests compassion-based therapies counteract the emotion dysregulation and self-judgment that maintain PTSD severity. Internal Family Systems (IFS) therapy is grounded in compassion, mindfulness, and contemplative inner dialogue. Though primarily an individual therapy for over 40 years, a group adaptation called PARTS (Program for Alleviating and Reducing...

item.title: The burden of bacterial antimicrobial resistance in the South Asia and high-income Asia-Pacific region over three decades: a systematic analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: This evaluation reveals divergent AMR burden trends between regions, highlighting the critical need for tailored interventions, particularly targeting the growing vulnerable aging population.

item.title: TMSB10 marks a malignant epithelial programme spatially associated with fibroblast-matrix niches in oral squamous cell carcinoma
item.description: CONCLUSION: Within malignant epithelial cells, TMSB10 expression is associated with a reproducible, pEMT-related programme spatially associated with CAF/ECM-rich regions. Knockdown findings support the involvement of TMSB10 in OSCC cell growth and migration.

item.title: Approaching canine inflammatory myopathy by cluster analysis: an immunohistopathological observational study
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Immune-mediated inflammatory myopathies (IMs) in dogs represent a heterogeneous group of disorders with incompletely characterized histopathological and immunophenotypic characteristics. This study aimed to identify multiparametric histological and immunophenotypic patterns in canine IMs to support accurate diagnosis from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) muscle biopsies.

item.title: Association of integrated nutritional guidance and mindfulness-based stress reduction with fertility outcomes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Receipt of integrated nutritional guidance and MBSR was associated with higher clinical pregnancy and confirmed-ovulation proportions and with more favorable metabolic and psychological changes than conventional care. Because treatment allocation was non-randomized, these findings should be interpreted as associations and require prospective confirmation.

item.title: Genome-wide association study of growth-related traits in mandarin fish (Siniperca chuatsi): identification of cross-trait associated loci and candidate genes using single-trait and multivariate linear mixed models
item.description: Mandarin fish (S. chuatsi) is China's most economically important freshwater aquaculture species, yet selective breeding remains constrained by long generation intervals and limited genomic resources. We performed whole-genome resequencing of 98 Siniperca chuatsi individuals (minimum 10-fold coverage), retaining 1,310,398 quality-controlled bi-allelic SNPs across 24 chromosomes. Population structure analysis (principal component analysis, neighbor-joining, and ADMIXTURE) resolved four primary...

item.title: Case Report: Multimodal treatment of pediatric H3G34-mutant diffuse hemispheric glioma: a safety and feasibility case report combining precision medicine and tumor treating fields with conventional care
item.description: Diffuse hemispheric glioma, H3G34-mutant (H3G34-DHG) is a rare, highly malignant brain tumour with a dismal prognosis and a median time to progression (TTP) of 10 months with best available practice. We report a case of a 13-year-old boy with H3G34-DHG who underwent a multimodal treatment strategy, combining backbone chemotherapy, radiotherapy, surgery, tumour treating fields with Wilms Tumour-1 (WT1) directed dendritic cell immunotherapy and targeted therapy (STAT3-inhibition). The patient had...

item.title: Disentangling environmental, irrigation, and clone effects on the cacao soil microbiome in a multi-location trial
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Plant-associated microbiomes can shape host phenotypes, yet plant breeding programs rarely incorporate microbiome data into their selection criteria. For example, multi-location trials are central for studying genotype-by-environment interactions, yet the microbiome is a poorly characterized component of environmental variation.

item.title: Growth/toxin-producing temperatures and comprehensive genomic dissection of two toxigenic Burkholderia gladioli pv. cocovenenans strains isolated from dried Auricularia auricula
item.description: The foodborne pathogen Burkholderia gladioli pv. cocovenenans (B. cocovenenans) produces the lethal mitochondrial toxin bongkrekic acid (BA). To more accurately assess the toxin production levels of toxigenic strains, it is necessary to further optimize the culture conditions used during laboratory detection procedures. Here, we characterized the temperature-dependent growth and BA production of two BA-producing B. cocovenenans strains isolated from commercially available dried Auricularia...

item.title: Spatial dynamics of systemic acquired resistance-associated metabolites in the wheat cultivar fielder infected by Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Systemic acquired resistance (SAR) is a whole-plant immune response in which localized pathogen attack primes distant tissues for enhanced defense. In Arabidopsis thaliana, this response is associated with the systemic accumulation of salicylic acid (SA), pipecolic acid (Pip), and N-hydroxypipecolic acid (NHP), but their spatial dynamics in wheat remain poorly understood.

item.title: Antimicrobial Resistance and Genomic Characteristics of Helicobacter pylori in Peptic Ulcer Disease: A Five-Case Series
item.description: CONCLUSION: This descriptive five-case series illustrates heterogeneous case-level antimicrobial susceptibility and genomic profiles in ulcer-associated H. pylori infection. The observations are not population-level resistance estimates, but they support the clinical value of culture-based susceptibility testing and/or validated molecular resistance detection for individualized management, particularly after prior eradication treatment.

item.title: Clinical phenotype and diagnostic pathways of 22q11.2 deletion syndrome in a Ukrainian cohort
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this Ukrainian cohort, 22q11.2DS diagnosis was predominantly phenotype-driven, with CHD representing the principal diagnostic trigger. Developmental delay was associated with diagnosis after 1 year, whereas immunological abnormalities relatively infrequently initiated diagnostic evaluation. Broader recognition of non-cardiac presentations, standardized referral criteria, coordinated multidisciplinary care, and continued development of newborn and prenatal screening may improve...

item.title: Habitat Suitability Assessment and Diurnal Activity Rhythms of the White-Cheeked Macaque (Macaca leucogenys) in Southeastern Xizang Based on the MaxEnt Model
item.description: The white-cheeked macaque (Macaca leucogenys) is primarily distributed in the Yarlung Zangbo Grand Canyon region of southeastern Xizang, but its habitat associations and temporal detection patterns remain poorly understood. Focusing on Gedang Township, Medog County, we combined camera-trap records collected from April 2023 to June 2025 with environmental predictors to assess habitat suitability using MaxEnt and to characterize diel and seasonal camera-trap detection patterns. The MaxEnt model...

item.title: Unraveling the role of MCM7 in cancer: a comprehensive analysis and functional validation from pan-cancer to lung adenocarcinoma
item.description: CONCLUSION: Our findings establish MCM7 as a bona fide pan cancer oncogenic determinant and a promising diagnostic/prognostic biomarker. Furthermore, we unveil a novel mechanistic axis linking MCM7 to JAK STAT3 driven inflammatory signaling in LUAD, offering a pre-clinical hypothesis for targeting MCM7 in combination with immunotherapeutic or JAK/STAT inhibitory regimens, although in-vivo validation and toxicity assessment remain essential.

item.title: Interactions between key bacterial microbiota and soil properties in healthy soils suppress tobacco bacterial wilt
item.description: Infections with Ralstonia solanacearum have caused considerable agricultural and economic losses. Complex interactions among pathogens, the soil microbiome and soil properties determine health status; however, their interactions have not been explored thoroughly. Here, we collected soils from local naturally healthy and diseased tobacco fields, used Illumina amplicon sequencing to analyze the soil microbial community, determined the physicochemical properties of the soils, and explored the...

item.title: From biomechanical data to robotic execution: design and control of an intelligent Tuina system
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) Tuina (massage) relies heavily on practitioners' physical stamina and subjective experience, leading to operational variability that hinders therapeutic standardization and scalable rehabilitation service delivery. To address this limitation, this study proposes an intelligent TCM Tuina robotic system integrating biomechanical data-driven design and hybrid control strategies.

item.title: Direct evidence of light-induced phase-fluctuations in cuprates via time-resolved ARPES
item.description: Light perturbation of the superconducting phase of cuprates typically promotes a non-thermal, superconducting-to-normal state phase transition. Although phase fluctuations are widely accepted as playing a primary role in disrupting long-range superconducting order, an experimental probe capable of unambiguously assessing their effect with momentum and time resolutions is still lacking. Here, by combining high-resolution time-resolved and temperature-dependent angle-resolved photoemission studies...

item.title: Acupuncture before and during letrozole ovulation induction in women with overweight or obesity and PCOS-related infertility: a randomized sham-controlled pilot trial
item.description: CONCLUSION: These preliminary findings suggest that continuous acupuncture spanning pretreatment and ovulation induction may be associated with a higher live-birth rate and improvements in metabolic and endometrial parameters. Given the exploratory nature and limited sample size of this pilot trial, confirmation in larger multicenter trials is required.

item.title: Intravascular lithotripsy vs. rotational atherectomy for severely calcified coronary lesions with concomitant tortuosity or angulation: a propensity-weighted real-world study from China
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort of patients with severely calcified coronary lesions, all of whom had concomitant tortuous or angulated anatomy, IVL was associated with a lower risk of one-year MACE compared with RA, an effect driven primarily by a reduction in heart failure rehospitalisation. The consistency across three analytical models suggests robustness of this finding, although confirmation in adequately powered randomised controlled trials is warranted.

item.title: Association of bilingual language use with brain age: MRI evidence from bilinguals, translators, and interpreters
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Professional bilingual experience was not robustly associated with age-corrected brain-age gap across pretrained models. Brain-age inference was sensitive to model choice and age-bias correction. BrainAge-specific interpreter patterns should therefore be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of a general difference in biological brain ageing.

item.title: Diagnostic spectrum and cytomorphological features of 1,641 pancreatobiliary EUS-FNA specimens: a five-year retrospective study from a central cytopathology laboratory serving 14 hospitals
item.description: CONCLUSION: EUS-FNA cytology provides clinically relevant information across a wide range of pancreatic and biliary tract lesions. This large, real-world cohort delineates the contemporary diagnostic spectrum of pancreatobiliary EUS-FNA cytology encountered in routine clinical practice and provides reference data on the distribution of cytological diagnostic categories, with a supplementary reclassification according to the WHO International System for Reporting Pancreaticobiliary Cytopathology....

item.title: Performance of the NightWatch seizure detection device on the leg compared to the standard arm placement: A pilot study
item.description: Nighttime monitoring is crucial for individuals with epilepsy, both to reduce the risk of injuries and to help prevent sudden unexpected death in epilepsy. NightWatch, a seizure detection device that can detect nocturnal seizures by using heart rate (HR) and movement parameters, has been shown to be effective when worn on the upper arm. This study piloted whether wearing NightWatch on the lower leg provides comparable seizure detection sensitivity. In this prospective pilot study, NightWatch...

item.title: Neoadjuvant anlotinib for locally advanced thyroid cancer: a single-arm phase II study (ALTER-T001)
item.description: CONCLUSION: Neoadjuvant anlotinib exhibited acceptable efficacy, tolerability, and QoL profiles in locally advanced DTC not amenable to surgery, with potential to reduce tumor burden and facilitate conversion surgery. Larger MTC cohorts are needed to further evaluate the efficacy and safety of neoadjuvant anlotinib.Clinical Trial Registration: https://www.chictr.org.cn/, identifier ChiCTR2100048077.

item.title: Adverse pregnancy outcomes and associated maternal and infection-related factors in a rural malaria-endemic setting in Western Kenya
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Maternal health during pregnancy is critical for favorable birth outcomes and long-term wellbeing of both mothers and infants. Women in rural, malaria-endemic regions face unique biological and socioeconomic challenges that may increase the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs). This study investigated the proportions and determinants of APOs among pregnant women attending antenatal care at Webuye sub-County Hospital in Western Kenya, a rural malaria-endemic setting.

item.title: Serum context shapes macrophage baseline state and LPS responsiveness in human monocyte-derived macrophages
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Serum context is a major determinant of macrophage baseline state and inflammatory responsiveness. FCS is associated with a more inflammatory baseline and attenuated LPS-induced activation, while AS shows a metabolically and immunologically homeostatic baseline with greater LPS responsiveness. These findings demonstrate that serum composition shapes basal macrophage programs and differentially modulates responses to inflammatory versus alternative stimulation, supporting...

item.title: Normative references of corpus callosum across lifespan and application in neurological and neuroimmunological disorders
item.description: CONCLUSION: Lifespan normative references of the CC provide a quantitative framework for characterizing individual structural deviations across neurological and neuroimmunological disorders. Exploratory clinical analyses suggest potential applications that require further validation.

item.title: Digital health misinformation in Southeast Asia: a systematic review of susceptibility, public health consequences, and intervention evidence
item.description: BACKGROUND: Digital health misinformation forms part of the information environment in which people assess health risks and act on health advice. We systematically reviewed participant-level studies from Southeast Asia addressing susceptibility, public-health consequences, and intervention evidence.

item.title: Emerging Multimodal AIE Theranostics with Key Diagnostic and Therapeutic Roles: A Review of Evidence
item.description: Chronic osteomyelitis and hard-to-heal wounds, including diabetic foot ulcers, are characterized by hypoxia, persistent biofilms, impaired antimicrobial penetration, and dysregulated inflammatory and regenerative responses, which together complicate diagnosis and treatment. Aggregation-induced emission (AIE)-based theranostic systems have emerged as experimental platforms that integrate fluorescence imaging with photodynamic, photothermal, catalytic, and tissue-regenerative functions....

item.title: Exploring the nexus of climate-socioeconomic drivers of dengue transmission: a covariate-augmented SEIR-SEI mechanistic model
item.description: A deterministic covariate-augmented SEIR-SEI model is developed and used to gain insight into the nexus between climate and socioeconomic parameters and the transmission dynamics of dengue. The model developed a framework that incorporates two external influences: climate and socioeconomic factors. The model is rigorously analyzed, with disease-free and endemic equilibria investigated, and is simulated using data relevant to Medellín, Colombia. We then employ machine learning algorithms as an...

item.title: pH-Responsive biomaterials for ROS regulation: from pathological mechanisms to design principles
item.description: Reactive oxygen species (ROS)-regulating biomaterials have been developed for diverse diseases. Their therapeutic value depends on the ROS species affected and the magnitude, direction, timing and location of redox intervention while preserving physiological signaling. Local pH deviations occur across diverse ROS-related pathological conditions and can influence biochemical processes that shape redox balance. Therefore, pathological pH is not merely a trigger for material activation, but a...

item.title: The Stanford Multifaceted Dissociation Questionnaire: A 9-Item Measure of Trait and State Dissociation
item.description: Dissociation is a common and increasingly studied phenomenon with substantial relevance for mental health. To date, researchers have often relied upon broad conceptualizations and retrospective measures, making it difficult to identify a consistent subset of experiences for dissociation, explore their links to related phenomena, and differentiate habitual from momentary dissociation. To address these issues, we introduce the Stanford Multifaceted Dissociation Questionnaire (SMDQ), a 9-item...

item.title: Immediate Return or Overnight Stay? Sleep Responses by Postmatch Travel Strategy and Match Participation in Professional Football
item.description: CONCLUSION: Neither travel strategy was uniformly superior. Overnight stay was associated with poorer absolute sleep duration but a clearer next-night rebound in sleep quality and duration.

item.title: Bismuth phosphanides Bi(PR2)3 react with chalcogens and P4: oxidation vs. transfer of the phosphanyl (PR2) unit
item.description: Simple, homoleptic bismuth phosphanides Bi(PR(2))(3) (R(2) = tBuCy, tBu(2)) have recently been introduced to the literature. With the aim of mapping the reactivity profiles of these interpnictogen compounds, reactions with elemental chalcogens (S(8), Se(grey), Te) and white phosphorus (P(4)) have been investigated. In these reactions, oxidation of the P atoms in the coordination sphere of bismuth is shown to compete with phosphanyl (PR(2)) transfer from bismuth to the group 15/16 element....

item.title: TFEB overexpression in excitatory neurons ameliorates amyloid-β pathology via coordinated enhancement of autophagy-lysosome and mitochondrial function
item.description: The intraneuronal accumulation of amyloid-β (Aβ) is an early pathogenic event in Alzheimer's disease (AD), initiating a pathological cascade that includes synaptic dysfunction, metabolic deficits, and eventual neuronal loss. Transcription factor EB (TFEB), a master regulator of the autophagy-lysosomal pathway (ALP) and mitochondrial homeostasis, represents a promising therapeutic target. However, its efficacy and mechanisms when specifically activated in neurons during the prodromal stage remain...

item.description: Fingerprint development has been a cornerstone of forensic science for over a century, with magnetic powders playing a critical role in visualizing latent prints on various surfaces. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: PD-L1 CPS may serve as a complementary, hypothesis-generating prognostic marker in colorectal adenocarcinoma, particularly for disease-free survival. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Anagliptin added to metformin and empagliflozin 10 mg provided confirmatory evidence of additional glycaemic efficacy in a separately randomised Korean population, increased glycaemic responder rates and improved estimated β-cell function, with acceptable short-term tolerability.

item.description: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is an aggressive malignancy characterized by poor prognosis and high recurrence rates. item.title: Comparative evaluation of ChatGPT-4o and ChatGPT-5.1 for automated LUTS scoring from clinician-documented narratives
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: ChatGPT-4o and ChatGPT-5.1 demonstrated comparable and moderate performance in approximating LUTS-related symptom scores from unstructured clinical narratives. These findings suggest that generative AI models may serve as supportive tools for automated symptom quantification and indicate relative performance stability across model generations within real-world urological practice.
